\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{گرفتار} \ur{کرنا} (giraftār karnā)}{گرفتار کرنا (giraftār karnā)}]{\ur{گرفتار} \ur{کرنا} (giraftār karnā) — to arrest}

\label{lesson:UR-C283-giraftar-karna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for proof, then the Urdu for to look for.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{گرفتار} \ur{کرنا}}
\textbf{\ur{گرفتار} \ur{کرنا}} — \emph{giraftār karnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to arrest\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{پولیس} \ur{نے} \ur{چور} \ur{کو} \ur{گرفتار} \ur{کیا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{polīs ne chor ko giraftār kiyā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The police arrested the thief.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{مجرم} \ur{کو} \ur{گرفتار} \ur{کیا}, \emph{us ne mujrim ko giraftār kiyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{گرفتار} \ur{کرنا}} (\emph{giraftār karnā}) is built from Persian \emph{giriftār}, \textquotedblleft{}seized, taken captive\textquotedblright{}, usually traced to the Persian verb for taking hold, and \textbf{\ur{کرنا}}. The person arrested takes \textbf{\ur{کو}}: \textbf{\ur{چور} \ur{کو} \ur{گرفتار} \ur{کیا}}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{giraftār karnā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{giraftār karnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{polīs ne chor ko giraftār kiyā.} — The police arrested the thief.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for proof, then the Urdu for to look for, then say \emph{giraftār karnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{گرفتار} \ur{کرنا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To arrest\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{عدالت} (adālat)}{عدالت (adālat)}]{\ur{عدالت} (adālat) — a court of law}

\label{lesson:UR-C283-adalat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to look for, then the Urdu for to arrest.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{عدالت}}
\textbf{\ur{عدالت}} — \emph{adālat} — \textquotedblleft{}a court of law\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{کل} \ur{عدالت} \ur{بند} \ur{تھی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kal adālat band thī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The court was closed yesterday.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{عدالت}} (\emph{adālat}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{ʿadāla}, \textquotedblleft{}justice, fairness\textquotedblright{}: the place where justice is done. It is feminine: \textbf{\ur{عدالت} \ur{بند} \ur{تھی}}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{adālat}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kal adālat band thī.} — The court was closed yesterday.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to look for, then the Urdu for to arrest, then say \emph{adālat} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{مقدمہ} (muqaddamā)}{مقدمہ (muqaddamā)}]{\ur{مقدمہ} (muqaddamā) — a court case; a lawsuit}

\label{lesson:UR-C283-muqaddama}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to arrest, then the Urdu for a court of law.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{مقدمہ}}
\textbf{\ur{مقدمہ}} — \emph{muqaddamā} — \textquotedblleft{}a court case; a lawsuit\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{مقدمہ} \ur{ایک} \ur{سال} \ur{چلا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{muqaddamā ek sāl chalā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The case went on for a year.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{مقدمہ}} (\emph{muqaddamā}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{muqaddama}, \textquotedblleft{}what is put first, a preface\textquotedblright{}; how it came to mean a court case is not certain. A case \textbf{\ur{چلتا} \ur{ہے}}: it goes on.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to arrest, then the Urdu for a court of law, then say \emph{muqaddamā} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{سزا} (sazā)}{سزا (sazā)}]{\ur{سزا} (sazā) — a punishment; a sentence}

\label{lesson:UR-C283-saza}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a court of law, then the Urdu for a court case.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{سزا}}
\textbf{\ur{سزا}} — \emph{sazā} — \textquotedblleft{}a punishment; a sentence\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{ثبوت} \ur{ہے} \ur{تو} \ur{سزا} \ur{ملے} \ur{گی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar subūt hai to sazā mile gī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If there is proof, there will be a sentence.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{سزا}} (\emph{sazā}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{sazā}, \textquotedblleft{}what is fitting, what one deserves\textquotedblright{}. It is feminine: \textbf{\ur{سزا} \ur{ملے} \ur{گی}}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ہتھکڑی} (hathkaṛī)}{ہتھکڑی (hathkaṛī)}]{\ur{ہتھکڑی} (hathkaṛī) — handcuffs}

\label{lesson:UR-C283-hathkari}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a court case, then the Urdu for a punishment.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ہتھکڑی}}
\textbf{\ur{ہتھکڑی}} — \emph{hathkaṛī} — \textquotedblleft{}handcuffs\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{چور} \ur{کے} \ur{ہاتھوں} \ur{میں} \ur{ہتھکڑیاں} \ur{تھیں۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{chor ke hāthoṅ meṅ hathkaṛiyāṅ thīṅ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The thief was in handcuffs.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{ہتھکڑی}} (\emph{hathkaṛī}) is built from \textbf{\ur{ہاتھ}}, a hand (CDIAL 14024), and \emph{kaṛī}, a metal ring, which CDIAL lists for Hindi under Sanskrit \emph{káṭa} (CDIAL 2629): rings for the hands. The first part shortens, as \textbf{\ur{ہاتھ}} does in compounds.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hathkaṛī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{chor ke hāthoṅ meṅ hathkaṛiyāṅ thīṅ.} — The thief was in handcuffs.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a court case, then the Urdu for a punishment, then say \emph{hathkaṛī} again
\end{itemize}

\section[(dialogue)]{Looking back: from A Theft in the Lane to The Case in Court}

\label{lesson:UR-R283-review-276-283}



\begin{quote}
Say the Urdu for a thief and a theft.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item a thief, a theft, to steal, a witness, a crime
  \item a pickpocket, to snatch, to swoop, on the run, a criminal
  \item a police inspector, a report (to the police), to register, a lock-up, a statement
  \item to recognize, a person's description, a suspicion, a scene, to be seen
  \item a bandit, an armed robbery, a gun, to tie up, a looter
  \item to cheat, a deception, a bribe, a crook, forged
  \item an investigation, a clue, a detective, proof, to look for
  \item to arrest, a court of law, a court case, a punishment, handcuffs
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
A thief? (\textbf{\ur{چور}}, \emph{chor}.) A theft? (\textbf{\ur{چوری}}, \emph{chorī}.) To steal? (\textbf{\ur{چرانا}}, \emph{churānā}.) A witness? (\textbf{\ur{گواہ}}, \emph{gavāh}.) A crime? (\textbf{\ur{واردات}}, \emph{vārdāt}.) A pickpocket? (\textbf{\ur{جیب} \ur{کترا}}, \emph{jeb katrā}.) To snatch? (\textbf{\ur{چھیننا}}, \emph{chhīnnā}.) To swoop? (\textbf{\ur{جھپٹنا}}, \emph{jhapaṭnā}.) On the run? (\textbf{\ur{فرار}}, \emph{farār}.) A criminal? (\textbf{\ur{مجرم}}, \emph{mujrim}.) A police inspector? (\textbf{\ur{داروغہ}}, \emph{dāroghā}.) A report (to the police)? (\textbf{\ur{رپورٹ}}, \emph{riporṭ}.) To register? (\textbf{\ur{درج} \ur{کرنا}}, \emph{darj karnā}.) A lock-up? (\textbf{\ur{حوالات}}, \emph{havālāt}.) A statement? (\textbf{\ur{بیان}}, \emph{bayān}.) To recognize? (\textbf{\ur{پہچاننا}}, \emph{pahchānnā}.) A person's description? (\textbf{\ur{حلیہ}}, \emph{huliyā}.) A suspicion? (\textbf{\ur{شبہ}}, \emph{shubah}.) A scene? (\textbf{\ur{منظر}}, \emph{manzar}.) To be seen? (\textbf{\ur{نظر} \ur{آنا}}, \emph{nazar ānā}.) A bandit? (\textbf{\ur{ڈاکو}}, \emph{ḍākū}.) An armed robbery? (\textbf{\ur{ڈاکہ}}, \emph{ḍākā}.) A gun? (\textbf{\ur{بندوق}}, \emph{bandūq}.) To tie up? (\textbf{\ur{باندھنا}}, \emph{bāndhnā}.) A looter? (\textbf{\ur{لٹیرا}}, \emph{luṭerā}.) To cheat? (\textbf{\ur{ٹھگنا}}, \emph{ṭhagnā}.) A deception? (\textbf{\ur{دھوکا}}, \emph{dhokā}.) A bribe? (\textbf{\ur{رشوت}}, \emph{rishvat}.) A crook? (\textbf{\ur{بدمعاش}}, \emph{badmāsh}.) Forged? (\textbf{\ur{جعلی}}, \emph{jālī}.) An investigation? (\textbf{\ur{تفتیش}}, \emph{taftīsh}.) A clue? (\textbf{\ur{سراغ}}, \emph{surāgh}.) A detective? (\textbf{\ur{جاسوس}}, \emph{jāsūs}.) Proof? (\textbf{\ur{ثبوت}}, \emph{subūt}.) To look for? (\textbf{\ur{ڈھونڈنا}}, \emph{ḍhūnḍnā}.) To arrest? (\textbf{\ur{گرفتار} \ur{کرنا}}, \emph{giraftār karnā}.) A court of law? (\textbf{\ur{عدالت}}, \emph{adālat}.) A court case? (\textbf{\ur{مقدمہ}}, \emph{muqaddamā}.) A punishment? (\textbf{\ur{سزا}}, \emph{sazā}.) Handcuffs? (\textbf{\ur{ہتھکڑی}}, \emph{hathkaṛī}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
